decisions.question: Reviewers rate findings P0 (blocking), P1 (should be fixed before approval) or P2 (optional). Does any finding here have to be fixed before this is approved?
Can every finding here be resolved by adding or clarifying text, without changing a figure, a rule, a date or the decision itself?

full.final:
REQ-1: For each year 7 student, the system evaluates two signals each school day: attendance percentage over the last 20 school days, and the count of failing grades in the current term.
REQ-2: A student is flagged at risk if either condition holds: attendance below 90% over the last 20 school days, OR two or more failing grades in the current term. Either condition alone is sufficient.
REQ-3: The flag is visible only to the student's assigned counsellor and the head of year 7; it is not shown to any other staff, the student, or parents.
REQ-4: The flag appears in the counsellor's and head of year's view on the school day the condition is first met, so follow-up can occur within a week.
REQ-5: The flag clears automatically when neither condition has held for 10 consecutive school days; it does not clear earlier, needs no manual action, and any recurrence of either condition within the window restarts the 10-day count.
AC-1: Student present 17 of the last 20 school days (85%) with no failing grades -> flagged, on the attendance condition alone.
AC-2: Student present 18 of the last 20 school days (exactly 90%) with one failing grade this term -> not flagged, because 90% is not below 90% and 1 is fewer than 2.
AC-3: Student present 20 of the last 20 school days (100%) with exactly two failing grades this term -> flagged, on the grades condition alone; the flag is visible to the counsellor and head of year 7 the same school day, leaving the rest of the week for follow-up.
AC-4: Student at 85% attendance with three failing grades (both conditions, grades above the threshold) -> flagged once, and remains flagged while either condition holds.
AC-5: For a flagged student, the assigned counsellor and the head of year 7 see the flag; a class teacher, office staff, the student, and a parent opening the same record see no flag and no indication one exists.
AC-6: A flagged student whose attendance returns to 92% and who has one failing grade: the flag is still shown on school day 9 after both conditions stopped holding, and clears automatically at the end of school day 10 provided neither condition recurred; if attendance drops to 88% on day 6, the 10-day count restarts from that day.

gated.final:
REQ-1: For each year 7 student, the system evaluates two signals each school day: attendance percentage over the last 20 school days, and count of failing grades in the current term.
REQ-2: A student is flagged at risk if either condition holds: attendance below 90% over the last 20 school days, or two or more failing grades in the current term. Either condition alone is sufficient, so the counsellor can follow up within a week.
REQ-3: The flag is visible only to the student's assigned counsellor and the head of year 7; it is not shown to any other staff, the student, or parents.
REQ-4: The flag clears automatically when neither condition has held for 10 consecutive school days; it does not clear earlier, a recurring condition restarts the count, and it needs no manual action.
AC-1: Student present 17 of the last 20 school days (85%) with no failing grades is flagged on the attendance condition alone; the flag is visible only to that student's counsellor and the head of year 7, not to teachers, office staff, the student, or parents.
AC-2: Student present 18 of the last 20 school days (exactly 90%) with one failing grade this term is not flagged, because 90% is not below 90% and 1 is fewer than 2.
AC-3: Student present 19 of the last 20 school days (95%) with three failing grades this term is flagged on the grades condition alone; a student present 17 of 20 (85%) with two failing grades is flagged because both conditions hold; the flag appears in the counsellor's and head of year's view the same school day, so follow-up can occur within a week.
AC-4: A flagged student at 19 of the last 20 school days (95%) with one failing grade still shows the flag on school day 9 after both conditions stopped holding, and the flag clears automatically at the end of school day 10 if neither condition recurred; if attendance is 17 of the last 20 (85%) on day 6, the 10-day count restarts.

errorsInVersion1: AC-3 tests the exactly-two-failing-grades boundary only in a case where attendance is also 85%, so both conditions hold at once; the minimum grade threshold is never isolated with passing attendance (one-grade no-flag and three-grade flag are covered, exactly two alone is not).

ACs bundle several distinct checks into one criterion (AC-3 covers grades-only, both-conditions and same-day timeliness), which weakens their use as discrete pass/fail tests, though no rule or figure is wrong.
errorsInVersion2: AC-6 uses 92% attendance over the last 20 school days; with a 20-day window only multiples of 5% are possible (18/20 = 90%, 19/20 = 95%), so this test case cannot be constructed.
AC-6 also uses 88% attendance on day 6; again not achievable over 20 school days (17/20 = 85%, 18/20 = 90%). The intent (below 90%) is clear but the figure is wrong.
REQ-4 and AC-3 establish same-day visibility to the counsellor but still define no notification mechanism, so 'reaches them in time' rests on the counsellor opening the view.
claude.reason: Version 2 covers the same rules and thresholds correctly but gives the two P1 gaps dedicated, independently testable coverage (REQ-4 for the within-a-week timeline and AC-5 for the negative visibility test) plus separate criteria for the exactly-two and three-grade cases, which outweighs its two impossible attendance percentages in AC-6 (92% and 88% are unattainable over a 20-day window).

grok.reason: Version 2 is better because it makes same-day counsellor visibility its own requirement and gives separate tests for unauthorized access, the exact two-grade boundary, three failing grades with both conditions, and a consecutive ten-day clear that restarts on recurrence, while Version 1 only embeds those checks in other cases.
